state.body: OK I'll try to keep this focused, though I've got about three things going on at once. Our company runs a B2B marketing platform and we have customer event data arriving from around forty integrations, most of them webhooks, some of them batch exports from customers' own data warehouses. We're on Postgres for the application and BigQuery for analytics. The glue between them is a mess: webhooks land in a queue, a worker writes raw JSON into a staging table, and then a set of dbt-like SQL scripts we wrote ourselves flatten it. I'd like to evaluate whether a managed ingestion layer with native webhook and warehouse-to-warehouse sync support would let us retire the custom worker and most of the flattening SQL.

state.body: My partner keeps telling me to stop working on weekends but here I am.
